stem: A 4-month-old infant has a small punctum on the side of the neck that intermittently discharges clear fluid. How far superiorly does this branchial fistula typically extend?

options.text: It ends blindly just deep to the skin surface.
To the base of the thyroid gland.
Up to the bed of the tonsil.

explanation: Branchial fistulas represent remnants of the branchial arches and commonly track up to the oropharynx at the tonsillar bed.
rationale: Think about the internal opening of this embryological remnant in the throat.

optionExplanations.A: If it ended blindly near the skin, it would be a sinus rather than a fistula that extends deep into the neck.
optionExplanations.B: The thyroid gland is related to thyroglossal remnants, whereas branchial remnants follow a different embryological path.
optionExplanations.C: Branchial fistulas represent remnants of the branchial arches and commonly track up to the oropharynx at the tonsillar bed.
optionExplanations.D: While first branchial arch remnants can relate to the ear, the typical cervical fistula described follows a path toward the tonsil.

source.hint: Think about the internal opening of this embryological remnant in the throat.
